answer: Burn-to-register resists sybil: every agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle and provably dissipate a fixed energy budget before its key is admitted, with the tally read from physical signatures rather than self-report. The attacker cost is joules actually burned: powering a thousand ghost identities draws real current through copper-wound transformers, throws a measurable thermal plume from the cooling stack, and sags the line enough to show voltage ripple at the meter. Each extra shell earns no discount; the energy ledger counts every watt-hour the farm spends, and none of it is refundable.
